mishnayos.summary: The Kohanim guarded the Beis HaMikdash at night in three places. This mishnah tells where they slept, and what a Kohen who became tamei at night did.

chunks.he: בִּשְׁלשָׁה מְקוֹמוֹת הַכֹּהֲנִים שׁוֹמְרִים בְּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ.
chunks.en: The Kohanim guard the Beis HaMikdash in three places:

words.note: The Beis HaMikdash, the Holy Temple in Yerushalayim.

chunks.en: in the Beis Avtinas room,

words.note: The family that made the ketores (incense); their room was named after them.

chunks.en: in the Beis HaNitzotz room, and in the Beis HaMoked room.

words.note: A room with a small fire always burning.
A room with a fire where the Kohanim warmed up.

chunks.he: בֵּית אַבְטִינָס וּבֵית הַנִּיצוֹץ הָיוּ עֲלִיּוֹת,
chunks.en: Beis Avtinas and Beis HaNitzotz had upstairs rooms,
and the young Kohanim guarded there.

words.note: Young Kohanim, not yet old enough to serve.

chunks.en: The Beis HaMoked
had a round dome roof, and it was a big hall,
with rows of stone benches all around.
The older Kohanim of the family serving the next day slept there,

words.note: Beis av: the family of Kohanim whose day it was to serve.

chunks.en: and they held the keys of the azarah.

words.note: The courtyard of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: The young Kohanim each slept with his blanket on the floor.
They did not sleep in the holy clothes.
Instead, they took them off, folded them, and put them
under their heads,
and covered themselves with their own clothes.
If one of them became tamei during the night,

words.note: Something that makes a Kohen tamei and unable to serve.

chunks.en: he goes out and walks through the tunnel
that goes under the Beis HaMikdash,

words.note: Here: the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: with lamps burning on this side and on that side,
until he reaches the room for tevilah.

words.note: Dipping in a mikvah to become tahor.

chunks.en: There was a fire there,
and a respectful bathroom.
And this was its respect:
If he found it locked,
he knows someone is in there.
If it was open, he knows no one is in there.
He went down and toveled,

words.note: Dipped in the mikvah.

chunks.en: came up, dried himself, and warmed up by the fire.
He came and sat down next to his brothers,
the Kohanim, until the gates were opened (in the morning),
and then he goes out on his way.
chunks.explain: He may not stay in the Beis HaMikdash until the day is over.

mishnayos.summary: Each morning a Kohen took the ashes off the mizbe'ach. Whoever wanted this job toveled early, and then they held a lottery to choose who would do it.

chunks.he: מִי שֶׁהוּא רוֹצֶה לִתְרֹם אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ,
chunks.en: Whoever wants to take the ashes off the mizbe'ach
chunks.st: whoever wants to remove the ashes from the altar

words.note: Here: to take the ashes off the mizbe'ach.
The altar.

chunks.he: מַשְׁכִּים וְטוֹבֵל עַד שֶׁלֹּא יָבֹא הַמְמֻנֶּה.
chunks.en: gets up early and tovels before the memuneh comes.
chunks.st: rises early and immerses himself in a ritual bath, as required of anyone who enters the Temple courtyard. He must immerse before the appointed priest arrives,
chunks.stMore: as the appointed priest oversees the lottery that determines which priests perform the various rites of the Temple service, and the first of those lotteries determines who will be charged with the removal of the ashes.

words.note: The Kohen in charge of the lotteries.

chunks.en: And at what time does the memuneh come?
chunks.st: And at what time does the appointed priest arrive?

chunks.en: Not every time is the same.
chunks.st: The times of his arrival are not all the same. There are

chunks.en: Sometimes he comes when the rooster crows,
chunks.st: times that he comes at the call of the rooster [hagever], or he might come at

chunks.he: אוֹ סָמוּךְ לוֹ מִלְּפָנָיו אוֹ מִלְּאַחֲרָיו.
chunks.en: or close to it, a little before or a little after.
chunks.st: an adjacent time, either before the call of the rooster or after it.

chunks.en: The memuneh comes and knocks on their door,
chunks.st: The appointed priest arrived at the Chamber of the Hearth, where the priests of the patrilineal family were assembled, and he knocked on the gate to alert them to open the gate for him.

chunks.en: and they open it for him.
chunks.st: And when they opened the gate for him,

chunks.en: He says to them,
chunks.st: he said to them:

chunks.en: "Whoever toveled may come and join the lottery."
chunks.st: Whoever immersed in the ritual bath may come and participate in the lottery.

chunks.en: They held the lottery, and whoever won, won (the job).
chunks.st: They then conducted the lottery, and whoever won that lottery won
chunks.stMore: the privilege to perform the rite of the removal of the ashes.

mishnayos.stIntro: The mishna describes the commencement of the daily service in the Temple: Among the members of the priestly family who are to serve in the Temple that day,

mishnayos.summary: The memuneh opened the door to the azarah, and the Kohanim walked around with torches to check that all the holy vessels were in place. Then the chavitin baker was set to work.

chunks.he: נָטַל אֶת הַמַּפְתֵּחַ וּפָתַח אֶת הַפִּשְׁפָּשׁ,
chunks.en: He took the key and opened the small door,
chunks.st: took the key that was kept beneath a marble tablet set in the floor of the Chamber of the Hearth and opened with it the wicket [hapishpesh] in the gate of the Chamber of the Hearth.

words.note: A little door inside the big gate.

chunks.en: and went in from the Beis HaMoked to the azarah.
chunks.st: And he entered through the wicket from the Chamber of the Hearth to the Temple courtyard;

chunks.en: The Kohanim went in after him with two fire torches
chunks.st: and the priests of the patrilineal family entered after him, and two torches of fire were

chunks.en: in their hands.
chunks.st: in their hands, to light the way.

chunks.en: They split into two groups.
chunks.st: The priests divided into two groups; these priests would

chunks.en: These walk along the covered walkway toward the east,
chunks.st: walk along the portico that surrounded the Temple courtyard, starting in the direction of east,

chunks.en: and these walk along the walkway toward the west.
chunks.st: and those priests would walk along the portico starting in the direction of west.
chunks.stMore: The priests would ensure that all the service vessels were in place, ready for use in the daily service.

chunks.en: They kept checking as they walked, until they reached
chunks.st: Both groups would continue inspecting the vessels until they reached

chunks.en: the place of the room where the chavitin were made.
chunks.st: the place where the Chamber of the Preparer of the High Priest’s daily Griddle-Cake Offering was located.

words.note: A flat flour offering baked each day for the Kohen Gadol.

chunks.en: When both groups got there,
chunks.st: When they reached that place, these priests and those priests

chunks.en: they said, "Shalom!" (It is all fine),
chunks.st: said to each other: It is well;

words.note: Here: it is fine.

chunks.en: "Everything is fine!"
chunks.st: all is well, and all the vessels are in place.

chunks.en: They set the chavitin makers to make the chavitin.
chunks.st: They then set the preparer of the griddle-cake offering to prepare the griddle-cake offering.

mishnayos.stIntro: At some time near dawn the appointed priest

mishnayos.summary: The Kohen who won the lottery washed his hands and feet from the kiyor, climbed the mizbe'ach in the dark, and scooped up some ashes. He put them in a special place on the floor.

chunks.en: Whoever won (the job of) taking the ashes off the mizbe'ach,
chunks.st: who won the lottery to remove the ashes from the altar

chunks.en: he takes the ashes off the mizbe'ach.
chunks.st: shall then remove the ashes.

chunks.en: And they say to him,
chunks.st: And the other priests say to him:

chunks.en: "Be careful not to touch the vessel
chunks.st: Be careful that you do not touch the vessel with which you perform the rite

chunks.he: עַד שֶׁתְּקַדֵּשׁ יָדֶיךָ וְרַגְלֶיךָ מִן הַכִּיּוֹר,
chunks.en: until you wash your hands and feet from the kiyor.
chunks.st: until you sanctify your hands and your feet from the Basin,
chunks.stMore: as a priest may not perform any service in the Temple before sanctifying his hands and feet. The priests would continue their reminders:

words.note: Washing hands and feet for the holy service.
The big copper washing basin in the azarah.

chunks.en: The fire pan is placed in the corner
chunks.st: The coal pan with which the ashes are removed is placed in the corner

chunks.en: between the ramp and the mizbe'ach,
chunks.st: between the ramp and the altar,

words.note: The sloped walkway going up to the mizbe'ach.

chunks.en: on the west side of the ramp."
chunks.st: on the western side of the ramp.

chunks.en: No one goes in with him,
chunks.st: No person would enter with the priest who was removing the ashes, as it was permitted to enter the area between the Entrance Hall of the Sanctuary and the altar only when performing the Temple service. And there was

chunks.en: and he has no lamp in his hand.
chunks.st: no lamp in his hand when he went to fetch the coal pan.

chunks.en: Instead, he walks by the light of the fire on the mizbe'ach.
chunks.st: Rather, he would walk by the light of the arrangement
chunks.stMore: of wood on the altar, upon which the portions of the offerings sacrificed the previous day were burned during the night.

words.note: The pile of wood burning on the mizbe'ach.

chunks.en: The others did not see him
chunks.st: The other priests would not see him, as the altar hid him from their sight,

chunks.en: and did not hear his voice,
chunks.st: nor could they hear the sound of his
chunks.stMore: steps. They were therefore unaware of his progress

chunks.en: until they heard the sound of the wooden wheel that
chunks.st: until they heard the sound of the wood that

chunks.en: Ben Katin made for the kiyor.
chunks.st: ben Katin crafted into a mechanism [mukhani] of pulleys that was used to sink the Basin
chunks.stMore: into flowing water during the night, so that its water would not be disqualified by remaining overnight. When the priests heard the sound of the pulleys raising the Basin from the water,

words.note: A Kohen Gadol who made this machine.
A pulley machine to lower and raise the kiyor.

chunks.en: Then they said, "It is time!"
chunks.st: they said to each other: The time for sanctifying hands and feet has come.

chunks.en: He washed his hands and feet from the kiyor,
chunks.st: The priest sanctified his hands and his feet with water from the Basin after he raised it.

chunks.he: נָטַל מַחְתַּת הַכֶּסֶף וְעָלָה לְרֹאשׁ הַמִּזְבֵּחַ,
chunks.en: took the silver fire pan, and went up to the top of the mizbe'ach.
chunks.st: He then took the silver coal pan from the corner between the ramp and the altar, and ascended to the top of the altar. The priest

chunks.en: He pushed the coals to this side and that side,
chunks.st: cleared the upper layer of coals to this side and to that side and

chunks.en: and scooped up some of the burnt-up coals from the middle.
chunks.st: scooped into the coal pan the inner coals that were completely consumed.

chunks.en: And he went down. He reached the floor,
chunks.st: He then descended the ramp. When he reached the floor, in the southeast of the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: turned his face to the north,
chunks.st: he turned his face toward the north.

chunks.he: הָלַךְ לְמִזְרָחוֹ שֶׁל כֶּבֶשׁ כְּעֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת.
chunks.en: and walked along the east side of the ramp about ten amos.
chunks.st: He would walk along the east side of the ramp toward the south side of the altar, walking a distance of about ten cubits
chunks.stMore: from the bottom of the ramp, which was twenty cubits from the altar.

words.note: An amah is about the length of an arm.

chunks.he: צָבַר אֶת הַגֶּחָלִים עַל גַּבֵּי הָרִצְפָה
chunks.en: He piled the coals on the floor,
chunks.st: He then heaped the coals upon the floor in a location

chunks.en: three tefachim away from the ramp,
chunks.st: three handbreadths distant from the ramp, in the

words.note: A tefach is about the width of a hand.

chunks.en: at the place where they put the crop of the bird korban,
chunks.st: place where the priests would place the crop of the bird burnt offering,

words.note: The food-pouch in a bird's neck, removed from a bird korban.

chunks.en: and the ashes of the inner mizbe'ach and the Menorah.
chunks.st: the ashes removed from the inner, golden altar, and the ashes removed from the Candelabrum.

words.note: The golden mizbe'ach inside, for the ketores.

mishnayos.summary: When the other Kohanim saw that the first Kohen had taken the ashes, they ran up the mizbe'ach too. They moved the leftover pieces of korbanos from the night to the sides.

chunks.en: His brothers saw that he went down,
chunks.st: The brethren of the priest who removed the ashes, i.e., the other members of the patrilineal family, saw that he had descended from the altar with the coal pan,

chunks.en: and they ran and came (to the kiyor).
chunks.st: and they would run and come to the Basin.

chunks.he: מִהֲרוּ וְקִדְּשׁוּ יְדֵיהֶן וְרַגְלֵיהֶן מִן הַכִּיּוֹר,
chunks.en: They hurried and washed their hands and feet from the kiyor,
chunks.st: They made haste and sanctified their hands and their feet with the water in the Basin, and then

chunks.en: took the shovels and the forks,
chunks.st: they took the shovels

chunks.en: and went up to the top of the mizbe'ach.
chunks.st: and the forks and ascended with them to the top of the altar.
chunks.stMore: The shovels were for shoveling the ashes to the center of the altar, while the forks were required to remove from the altar those limbs that had not been consumed.

chunks.en: The pieces of the korbanos and the fats that did not burn up from the night before,
chunks.st: With regard to the limbs of burnt offerings and the fats of other offerings that had not been consumed and burned to ashes during the time from the previous evening, the priests would

words.note: Pieces of the korban olah.

chunks.en: they push them to the sides of the mizbe'ach.
chunks.st: clear them to the sides of the altar.

chunks.en: If the sides do not have room for them,
chunks.st: If the remaining limbs and fats were so abundant that the sides of the altar were unable to hold them, the priests would

chunks.en: they line them up on the ramp, across from the ledge.
chunks.st: arrange them on the ramp, opposite the surrounding ledge of the altar.

words.note: The sovev, a ledge that goes around the mizbe'ach.

mishnayos.stIntro: The previous mishna described the performance of the removal of the ashes by the priest who was selected to perform this task. This mishna continues:

mishnayos.summary: The Kohanim piled the ashes onto a big round heap in the middle of the mizbe'ach. On Yom Tov they left the heap there, because it made the mizbe'ach look beautiful.

chunks.he: הֵחֵלּוּ מַעֲלִין בָּאֵפֶר עַל גַּבֵּי הַתַּפּוּחַ.
chunks.en: They began to bring the ashes up onto the tapuach.
chunks.st: began raising the ashes onto the circular heap upon which the ashes were piled.

words.note: A big round heap of ashes on the mizbe'ach.

chunks.en: The tapuach was in the middle of the mizbe'ach.
chunks.st: The circular heap was in the middle of the altar.

chunks.en: Sometimes there were about three hundred kor of ashes on it.
chunks.st: Sometimes there was as much as three hundred kor of ashes upon it.
chunks.stMore: When the heap of ashes became excessively large, the priests would remove the ashes and pour them outside the city.

words.note: A very big measure.

chunks.en: On Yom Tov they did not clear it away,
chunks.st: But during the Festivals they would not remove the ashes from the altar,

chunks.en: because it is a beauty for the mizbe'ach.
chunks.st: as the ashes were considered an adornment to the altar,
chunks.stMore: since they were a sign of the great number of offerings that were sacrificed on it.

chunks.en: In all its days, the Kohen was never lazy
chunks.st: In all the days of the altar, even when there was an abundance of ashes upon it, the priest tasked with removing the ashes from the circular heap was never indolent

chunks.en: about taking out the ashes.
chunks.st: in removing the ashes.

mishnayos.summary: The Kohanim began to bring up logs to build the fire on the mizbe'ach. Any kind of wood may be used except olive and grapevine, but they usually used fig, nut, and pine wood.

chunks.he: הֵחֵלּוּ מַעֲלִין בְּגִזְרִין לְסַדֵּר אֵשׁ הַמַּעֲרָכָה.
chunks.en: They began to bring up logs to set up the fire on the mizbe'ach.
chunks.st: began raising logs onto the altar in order to assemble the arrangement of wood on which the offerings were burned.

words.note: The pile of wood burning on the mizbe'ach.

chunks.en: Is every kind of wood good for the fire?
chunks.st: The tanna asks: And is wood from all the trees fit for the arrangement?

chunks.en: Yes, every kind of wood is good for the fire,
chunks.st: The tanna replies: Wood from all the trees is fit for the arrangement,

chunks.en: except olive wood and grapevine wood.
chunks.st: except for wood from the vine and from the olive tree,

chunks.en: But they usually used these:
chunks.st: but the priests were accustomed to assemble the arrangement with wood from these trees:

chunks.en: young branches of fig trees, and of
chunks.st: With young branches of the fig tree, of the

chunks.en: nut trees, and of pine trees.
chunks.st: nut tree, and of pinewood.

words.note: Pine wood.

mishnayos.stIntro: After the ashes were cleared to the middle of the altar, the priests

chunks.en: He set up the big ma'arachah on the east side,
chunks.st: assembled the large arrangement of wood upon which the daily offering and the sacrificial portions of the other offerings are burned. It was assembled on the eastern side of the altar,

chunks.st: and its opening was on the eastern side of the altar,

chunks.he: וְרָאשֵׁי הַגִּזְרִין הַפְּנִימִיִּם הָיוּ נוֹגְעִים בַּתַּפּוּחַ.

chunks.en: There was space between the logs,
chunks.st: And there was space between the logs, in which the priests placed twigs,

mishnayos.stIntro: The priest who removed the ashes then

chunks.en: with enough wood to make five se'ahs of coals.
chunks.st: of an amount of wood estimated to produce five se’a of coals.

chunks.en: And on Shabbos, with enough to make eight se'ahs of coals,
chunks.st: And on Shabbat, it was assembled of an amount of wood estimated to produce eight se’a of coals,

chunks.en: because there they put the two bowls of
chunks.st: as there the priests would place the two bowls of

chunks.en: The pieces of the korbanos and the fats that did not burn up from the night before,
chunks.st: With regard to the limbs and the fats that were not consumed during the time from the previous evening, the priests would

chunks.en: they put them back on the big ma'arachah.
chunks.st: return them to the large arrangement to be burned.

chunks.en: They lit the two ma'arachos with fire,
chunks.st: And the priests kindled those two arrangements with fire and

chunks.en: and went down and came to the Lishkas HaGazis.
chunks.st: descended from the altar. And they then came to the Chamber of Hewn Stone,
chunks.stMore: where they would conduct the second lottery in order to determine who would perform the subsequent rites.

mishnayos.summary: The memuneh held a second lottery to choose who would do each job for the korban tamid: shechting, sprinkling the blood, cleaning the inner mizbe'ach and the Menorah, and carrying up each part of the korban.

chunks.en: The memuneh said to them,
chunks.st: The priest appointed to oversee the lotteries said to the priests:

chunks.en: "Come and join the lottery, (to see):
chunks.st: Come and participate in the lottery to determine

chunks.en: who shechts (the korban tamid),
chunks.st: who is the priest who will slaughter the daily offering;

chunks.en: who sprinkles (its blood),

chunks.en: and the two sides,

chunks.en: the insides, and the flour,
chunks.st: a sixth the innards; and a seventh the fine flour from the accompanying meal offering;

words.note: Fine flour of the mincha that comes with the korban.

chunks.en: and the chavitin, and the wine."
chunks.st: and an eighth the griddle-cake offering; and a ninth the wine for the libation.

words.note: The flat flour offering of the Kohen Gadol.
Wine poured on the mizbe'ach with the korban.

chunks.en: They held the lottery, and whoever won, won.
chunks.st: They conducted the lottery to determine the thirteen tasks, i.e., slaughtering, carrying the nine items or pairs of items, sprinkling the blood, removing the ashes from the inner altar, and removing the ashes from the Candelabrum. And whoever won that lottery won
chunks.stMore: the right to perform the slaughter, and the twelve priests standing to his right won the other privileges.

mishnayos.stIntro: Four lotteries were conducted in the Temple each day in order to determine which priests would perform which of the Temple rites. After describing the first of the lotteries, for removal of the ashes, the tanna describes the second lottery.

mishnayos.summary: Before shechting the korban tamid, the memuneh sent someone to check if it was daytime yet. The one who looked would call out when the sky in the east was light.

chunks.en: The memuneh said to them,
chunks.st: said to the priests:
